fixes.explanation: Gold does show up in this passage, but later. In verse 13, Sheba, Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish ask Gog whether he has come "…to make off with silver and gold…" In verse 4, what comes out with him is his army. So gold isn't what God says He will bring him out with.

This passage doesn't mention Gog's gods at all. Verse 4 says God will bring him out with all his army. Then it lists horses, horsemen in full armor and a great company with shields and bucklers. That list is soldiers and gear.

Sheba and Dedan do show up in this passage, but verse 8 doesn't name them as the ones on the mountains of Israel. In verse 13, they and the merchants of Tarshish ask a question about loot. The people verse 8 names are the ones gathered from many nations.

The text doesn't say that. God describes the people of that land as ones who "…all now dwell securely." Gog also calls them "…a quiet people who dwell securely…" Fear isn't the word either of them uses.
Merchants do come up in this passage, but Gog's plan isn't a trade deal. God says he will devise an evil plan. The merchants of Tarshish and the others only ask him about loot later in verse 13.

That's it. Gog says he will come against "…a land of unwalled villages…" and a quiet people, "…all of them living without walls or bars or gates…" Those are his own words about the people he plans to attack.
True. Gog says he will go "…in order to seize the spoil and carry off the plunder…" Those words are part of the plan God says he will say in verse 12. He says it plainly, about the quiet land.
False is right, baker. God says Gog will come "…from your place out of the far north…" with many peoples. They're all riding horses. The direction God gives is north, not south.

Prophets, yes. God asks if Gog is the one "…of whom I have spoken in former days through My servants, the prophets of Israel…" So God's question points back to what He spoke in former days through the prophets. The text says they prophesied for years in those times.

True. God says, "Now on that day when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, My wrath will flare up." It's a heavy line, so I'll say it plainly. The timing is the point: it's on the very day Gog comes against the land.

The sun and moon aren't in the list. God names the fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the beasts of the field, every creature that crawls upon the ground, and all mankind. Those are the ones who "…will tremble at My presence."

The text says the opposite. God says, "The mountains will be thrown down, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground." The verse says every wall, not just some of them. Mountains and cliffs come down too.

That's right. God says, "And I will summon a sword against Gog on all My mountains, declares the Lord GOD, and every man’s sword will be against his brother." It's a heavy line. The swords are turned on brothers.

The merchants of Tarshish show up back in verse 13, where they ask their question. In verse 21 God says, "…every man’s sword will be against his brother." So the verse names a brother, not the merchants, as what each sword is against.

Nineveh isn't in this passage. It's the city God told the prophet Jonah to go to (Jonah 1:2; 2 Kings 14:25). Here God says the torrents of rain, hailstones, fire and sulfur fall "…on him and on his troops and on the many nations with him." That means Gog and the ones who came with him.
